chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Recording with Mildred Bailey in Chicago and New York
summary: Bailey wanted Roy Eldridge, Teddy Wilson and Collins on her dates, recorded with the Three Deuces band in Chicago, and gave parties for musicians.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And I might add that during this same time I was doing quite a bit of recording with Mildred Bailey. She kept -- she always wanted Roy, Teddy Wilson and myself with her. It's a marvelous dates because we did some things with I think the writer was Alec Wilder, and she did some very good things during this time. And we used to have some great parties at our house. She loved to give parties and have all the musicians over. And Kenny Clark@ I think did quite a few recordings with her at this time. Also --
This was around 1940, around the same time that was I was rehearsing with Prez and just working with Benny. Quite busy, not making too much money, but quite busy. And --

That escaped me. I can't remember, and I have some --- I'm sure I have quite a few of the 78's at home. Maybe it'll come to me just a little later. But any way I did quite a few recordings with Mildred, as a matter of fact I recorded with Mildred in Chicago before I left Chicago to go to New York. She used to come to the Three Deuces all

the time, and she loved the band, and she recorded with our band. The only addition to our band at that time was Herbie Haymer, who was quite a saxophone player. He was working with she and Red Norver.

We did some tunes, 'Are You Looking At Me,' I can't think of all the tunes but they were very good. And when I went to New York I got in touch with her and we started recording together again. And I recorded as you know, I told you I recorded with Lady Day, did quite a few things with her. One record I did with her was done -- was arranged and conducted by Don Redman, an all star band also. And Georgie Auld, Byas, Don Byas, Roy Eldridge, Kenny Clark, there was just -- and when Kenny didn't make it I think Sid Catlett. It was quite a band.
